_comment: A sea standing far above the level the terrain left it -- the first half of the deep-ocean material's
**It steers a parameter that already existed and had never been used.** `Sea.DEPTH` has been the
aspect's one lever over height since the aspect was written, and no word in the corpus reached it. What
changed for this is not the parameter but its curve: the mapping is cubic, so the middle of the range
is still the twelve-block coastal trim it always was and only the ends reach an abyss.
**Its low end was a dud and was raised -- measured 2026-09-10** (`:common:oceandepth`). The span was
0.75..0.95, which the cubic turns into +40..+82 blocks; at +40 the share of columns clearing deep
water's threshold is **zero on every landform in the pack**, so half the word's range produced no abyss
at all and a writer got one or not on a seed roll they cannot see. 0.85..0.98 is +59..+90, and the
flat-floored shapes (`insular`, `archipelagic`, `eroded`) are then abyssal across nearly their whole sea at
**Still deliberately short of the extreme.** 0.98 is about 90 blocks up rather than the full 96, so
there is room left for a stronger word later: a word meaning `deep` should not also be the deepest
**It pushes `empty` away rather than admitting a pool.** A sea of nothing holds a depth perfectly well;
the result is simply invisible, so this is a preference and belongs where preferences do (`Sea.DEPTH`
records the same reasoning from the other side). Nothing here restricts, so the word never eliminates
